title: TechnologyEvent
description: A technology behavior element that denotes a discrete, instantaneous state change in infrastructure or platform software, such as an alert firing, a node or container failing, a scheduled trigger elapsing, or a deployment completing, that starts or results from technology functions, processes or interactions. It has no duration and performs no work itself. Use TechnologyProcess instead when the element is the multi-step job or pipeline that runs (backup job, deployment pipeline) rather than the trigger that starts it or the completion signal it emits. Use TechnologyFunction instead when the element is a continuous automated capability of a node (health checking, log rotation, load balancing) rather than a single occurrence detected or produced by it. Use TechnologyService instead when the element is the exposed monitoring, alerting or scheduling capability (Alertmanager, EventBridge, a cron service) that emits or delivers events, not the event itself. Use Artifact instead when the element is the file that declares the event condition, such as an alert-rule YAML, crontab or CloudWatch alarm template, rather than the state change it describes.

documentation.description: Free-text description of the state change: the condition that raises the event, its emitting source, and what it triggers. Set it whenever the event name alone does not make the trigger condition clear.

eventType.description: Technology state change category, per ArchiMate 3.2 Technology Event element; aligned with OpenTelemetry event semantics.

x-dr-evidence: A named alerting rule or alarm definition, such as a Prometheus rule with alert:, expr: and for: fields, a CloudWatch/Azure Monitor alarm, or a Datadog monitor, that fires on a metric threshold or failure condition.
A schedule trigger that starts infrastructure work, such as a Kubernetes CronJob schedule: field, a crontab line, a CI on: schedule block, or an EventBridge/Cloud Scheduler rule.

A handler subscribed to infrastructure lifecycle notifications, such as a Kubernetes watch on Pod/Node events, the Docker events API, a CI on: deployment_status trigger, a SIGTERM/preStop hook, or a webhook receiving deployment-completed payloads.
